Tapeinophrosune
ta-pay-no-fro-soo-NAY
n. (Greek)
Greek tapeinophrosunē, “lowliness of mind,” from tapeinos (low, lowly) + phronē (mind, way of thinking). The composite literally means “low-mindedness” in the inverted-from-modern-usage sense of thinking-of-oneself-as-low.

📖 Biblical Definition

Tapeinophrosunē is the New Testament’s precise word for humility of mind—the inward disposition that thinks of oneself accurately (which in fallen creatures saved by grace means: low) before God and esteems others better than self before men. The word is composite: tapeinos means low, lowly, and phronē means mind or way of thinking; together they name a low-mindedness that, in modern English, has acquired the opposite sense of mean or petty—but in Greek and in apostolic usage carries the entirely positive sense of thinking-of-oneself-as-low. The word is structural to several apostolic passages. Philippians 2:3: let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves—tapeinophrosunē as the explicit antidote to strife and vainglory. The verse leads into the Christological hymn of vv. 6-8 where Christ Himself models the disposition: who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Ephesians 4:2: with all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love—tapeinophrosunē as the first of the four virtues by which the unity of the Spirit is kept in the bond of peace. Acts 20:19: Paul describes his own ministry as serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations. Colossians 3:12: put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering. 1 Peter 5:5: likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility—the verb egkomboōmai means to tie on like an apron, picturing humility as the garment the saint puts on visibly in his dealings with others. The category is therefore precise. It is inward (a way of thinking, phronē): the actual estimate one holds of oneself before God. It is low (tapeinos): the regenerate soul, knowing both its sin and the grace by which it was saved, thinks of itself in low terms. It is consistent (a settled disposition, not occasional acts): the inward state that produces the outward life. And it is supremely Christ-shaped: the One who took the form of a servant, humbled Himself, and was obedient unto death is the model, and the conformity to His image is the long arc of the saint’s sanctification.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines HUMILITY (the closest English equivalent of tapeinophrosunē) as freedom from pride and arrogance; humbleness of mind; modest estimate of one’s own worth; in scripture, the inward Spirit-wrought disposition modeled supremely on Christ’s own self-humbling.

expand to see more

HUMILITY, n. — In ethics, freedom from pride and arrogance; humbleness of mind; a modest estimate of one’s own worth. In theology, that lowness of mind which is the disposition of the saint redeemed by grace, having a just sense of his sin and of God’s mercy in Christ. In lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves (Phil 2:3).

TAPEINOPHROSUNE — (Greek term.) Lowliness of mind; humility; the inward Spirit-wrought disposition of thinking-of-oneself-as-low. Found at Phil 2:3; Eph 4:2; Acts 20:19; Col 2:18, 23 (in counterfeit form); 3:12; 1 Pet 5:5.

📖 Key Scripture

Philippians 2:3 — "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves."

Ephesians 4:2 — "With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love."

Colossians 3:12 — "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering."

1 Peter 5:5 — "Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Tapeinophrosunē is corrupted, on one side, by the assertiveness-culture of the present age that has redefined humility as weakness and trained the believer to despise the very disposition Christ Himself models—and on the other by the false humility Paul explicitly warns against in Col 2:18, 23 (the performed self-deprecation that retains the inward pride while displaying the outward token).

expand to see more

The assertiveness-culture corruption is the most pervasive contemporary one. The cultural script is clear: lean in, know your worth, assert yourself, refuse to be made small, take up space. The Spirit-shaped disposition Paul commands—in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves—sounds to such ears like an invitation to weakness and oppression. But the inversion is the inner shape of the kingdom, modeled by the King who, being in the form of God, took upon Himself the form of a servant. The cure is the Christological pattern: the Christ-shaped soul learns that the way up in the kingdom is down, that the great are the servants, that he who humbles himself shall be exalted. Recover the doctrine, and the saint recovers also the freedom and dignity of the lower seat—the freedom from the exhausting labor of self-promotion and the dignity of walking the road his Master walked.

The opposite corruption is the false humility (literally, in Col 2:18, ethelothrēskia — will-worship paired with tapeinophrosunē) that Paul explicitly warns against: the performed self-deprecation that retains the inward pride while displaying the outward token. The performed humility takes various forms: the carefully curated self-deprecation that announces its own modesty; the boast disguised as confession (my biggest weakness is that I work too hard); the ascetic display that uses external rigor to flatter the soul; the visible token of low estimation offered for social credit. Paul names it precisely because it counterfeits the real virtue. The cure is the inward work: confess what is actually true, take the lower seat in reality, esteem others better in fact, refuse the inward boast that the performance was meant to mask. Recover both ends. Refuse the assertiveness-culture that despises the very disposition Christ models, and refuse the performed false humility that retains the inward pride. The biblical tapeinophrosunē is the inward thing, all the way through—the actual estimate of oneself before God, settled into the consistent disposition that produces both the words and the life of one conformed in measure to the lowly Christ.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek tapeinophrosunē from tapeinos (low) + phronē (mind, way of thinking): the inward Spirit-wrought disposition of thinking-of-oneself-as-low, modeled supremely on Christ’s own self-humbling (Phil 2:3-8), structural to apostolic ethics.

expand to see more

Greek tapeinophrosunē (G5012) — lowliness of mind, humility (Acts 20:19; Eph 4:2; Phil 2:3; Col 2:18, 23; 3:12; 1 Pet 5:5).

Greek tapeinos (G5011) — low, lowly, humble (the adjective; used of Christ’s heart in Matt 11:29).

Greek tapeinoō (G5013) — to make low, humble (James 4:10; 1 Pet 5:6; Phil 2:8 of Christ’s self-humbling).

Greek phronē (G5424) — understanding, mind (the second element of the compound).

Usage

"In lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves—Paul’s explicit command leading directly into the Christological hymn of Phil 2:6-11."

"Tapeinophrosunē is the inward state (a way of thinking, phronē) that produces the outward life; the actual estimate of oneself before God, not the performance for human view."

"Assertiveness-culture redefines humility as weakness; false humility performs the token while retaining the inward pride; biblical tapeinophrosunē is the Christ-shaped inward disposition, all the way through."
